s: a tiled, no-frills lokanta serving Istanbul home cooking since 2007
w: A traditional lokanta behind the Karaköy docks, serving daily-changing meze, stews and grilled dishes with the kind of consistency that has built a loyal regular crowd even as the neighbourhood around it gentrified. Blue-and-white tiled walls, brisk service, and food that tastes like it was made for the people eating it rather than for a menu photograph.
_facts: Located at Kemankeş Caddesi No:37, Karaköy, Beyoğlu, Istanbul
Opened in 2007, styled as a classic Istanbul lokanta (daily-changing home-style eatery)
Known for meze, seasonal vegetable dishes and grilled meats
Has featured in the Michelin Guide Istanbul

s: the world's first two-Michelin-star Turkish restaurant
w: Chef Fatih Tutak's tasting-menu restaurant reworks Turkish terroir -- Anatolian grains, foraged herbs, live-fire cooking -- into a two-Michelin-star experience, the first ever awarded to a Turkish restaurant. Dinner starts in ALVU, a lounge with panoramic Istanbul views, before moving to an intimate room where diners watch the kitchen work.
_facts: Located in Bomonti, Şişli, Istanbul
Run by chef Fatih Tutak, built around Turkish ingredients, terroir and live-fire technique
First restaurant in Turkey to hold two Michelin stars
Dining sequence begins in an adjoining lounge, ALVU, before moving to the main room

s: a cezve-brewed Turkish coffee institution up a passage off İstiklal since 1967
w: A tiny, standing-room coffee house tucked in a passage off İstiklal Caddesi, making Turkish coffee the traditional way in a copper cezve since 1967 -- thick, foam-capped, and strong enough that its name (roughly "the water buffalo won't sink") is a joke about its intensity. No frills, no seating to speak of, just a queue of regulars who consider it the city's benchmark cup.
_facts: Located at İstiklal Caddesi, Olivia Geçidi No:1/A, Beyoğlu, Istanbul
Trading since 1967
Makes traditional Turkish coffee in a copper cezve, known for its thick foam
Name translates roughly to "the water buffalo won't sink", a joke about the coffee's strength

s: a third-generation family coffee roaster trading in Fatih's Malta Bazaar since 1961
w: A dry-coffee roaster and shop run by the same family since 1961, now in its third generation under Selim Dönmez, in the historic Malta Çarşısı market in Fatih. The name has nothing to do with the country of Malta -- it's just the bazaar's name -- but the coffee, roasted and ground the traditional way, has kept neighbourhood regulars coming for over sixty years.
_facts: Located at İslambol Caddesi No:10, Ali Kuşçu, Fatih, Istanbul, inside the historic Malta Çarşısı (Malta Bazaar)
Family-run dry-coffee (kurukahve) roastery trading since 1961
Now run by Selim Dönmez, third generation of the founding family
Named for its Malta Bazaar location, unrelated to the country of Malta

s: a century-old nargile garden inside a 300-year-old Ottoman medrese courtyard
w: A lantern-strung courtyard nargile café set inside the Çorlulu Ali Paşa Medresesi, an early 18th-century Ottoman theological school just off the tram line near the Grand Bazaar. Students' cells around the courtyard now house low tables where locals and regulars linger for hours over tea, coffee and water pipes -- a genuinely old ritual in a genuinely old room, rather than a version built for visitors.
_facts: Located within the Çorlulu Ali Paşa Medresesi courtyard, Yeniçeriler Caddesi, Beyazıt, Fatih, Istanbul
The medrese (Islamic school) building dates to 1708-1710, commissioned by Grand Vizier Çorlulu Ali Pasha
Café has operated in the courtyard for around a century
Open late, on the tram line between Çemberlitaş and Beyazıt/Grand Bazaar

s: a hilltop café above the Golden Horn, named for the French novelist who used to sit here
w: A hilltop café reached by cable car or a walk through the Eyüp cemetery, named for French naval officer and novelist Pierre Loti, who is said to have written here overlooking the Golden Horn in the 19th century. Tea and Turkish coffee are secondary to the view -- one of Istanbul's classic panoramas, best at sunset with the water below and the old city receding into haze.
_facts: Located on a hilltop above the Eyüp cemetery, Eyüpsultan, Istanbul, overlooking the Golden Horn
Named after French writer Pierre Loti, who frequented a café on this hill in the 19th century
Reached by cable car (teleferik) from Eyüp or a walking path through the historic cemetery
Known as one of Istanbul's classic panoramic viewpoints, especially at sunset

s: a specialty roaster-cafe in Kadıköy's arty Yeldeğirmeni district
w: A precise, well-sourced specialty coffee bar in Yeldeğirmeni, the century-old-building, street-art-covered pocket of Kadıköy that's become a hub for Istanbul's creative Asian-side scene. Filter and espresso get the same seriousness here as the city's older cezve culture gets across the water -- part of a maturing third-wave scene that now runs alongside, rather than against, Turkish coffee tradition.
_facts: Located on Güneşlibahçe Sokak, Caferağa/Yeldeğirmeni, Kadıköy, Istanbul
Specialty coffee roaster-cafe in the Yeldeğirmeni neighbourhood
Yeldeğirmeni is known for early-20th-century architecture and community street art
Part of Istanbul's growing third-wave/specialty coffee scene on the Asian side
